newsitem.title: USA: Israeli official opposes U.S. strike against Iran.
newsitem.headline: Israeli official opposes U.S. strike against Iran.

text.p: A senior Israeli official said on Thursday it would be a serious mistake for the United States to take military action against Iran in retaliation for the bombing of U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia last year.

U.S. media reports say the Clinton administration could face strong domestic pressure to launch a military strike on Iran if hard evidence emerges of an Iranian role in the blast that killed 19 U.S. servicemen in Dhahran last June.

But Uri Lubrani, coordinator of Israeli activities in south Lebanon and an expert on Iran, told the Washington Institute for Near East Policy that such a move would rally ordinary Iranians behind their leaders.
Asked if a U.S. military response would have a counter-productive effect in Iran, Lubrani said: "Absolutely."

"(There is) no doubt in my mind that it will unite the people of Iran behind the ayatollahs ... because the 'patrie' (fatherland) is in danger. That is what will happen," he told the influential think-tank.
Even Iranian exiles opposed to the country's religious leadership had called for support for Iran when it was attacked by Iraq in 1980, he said.

U.S. officials say that so far they have no firm evidence that Iran was behind the blast, but more details could come to light if Canada decides to deport to the United States a Saudi man currently in custody there. Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh has been mentioned as possibly the driver of the truck used in the bombing.
Lubrani said Saudi authorities had been slow to reveal details of their investigation into the explosion because of their fear of Iranian retaliation.

Turning to south Lebanon, Lubrani said Israeli forces in a so-called "security zone" there to protect Israel's northern border faced an "unwinnable war" against Hizbollah guerrillas as long as Iran continued to finance and arm the group.
"As of April this year they have had, I think, 37 jumbo flights from Tehran to Damascus, full of arms, some of them much more sophisticated than have yet been used in Lebanon, to Hizbollah," he said.
Lubrani did not make clear over what period the arms had arrived in the Syrian capital. Israel says Syria's 35,000 troops in Lebanon connive at Hizbollah activities there.
